title: Inquest called into fatal police shooting near Brockville
subtitle: An inquest will be held into the shooting death of a mentally ill man by the Ontario Provincial Police near Brockville two years ago.
article: An inquest will be held into the shooting death of a mentally ill man by the Ontario Provincial Police near Brockville two years ago.

Matthew Roke, 33, was killed May 2, 2012 when he confronted two OPP officers in Maitland, Ont. Roke was threatening the officers with a knife and had lunged toward them when he was shot, according to Ontario's Special Investigations Unit, which cleared the officers of any wrongdoing.
Both officers fired their pistols and Roke was struck with four bullets.

Roke's parents had called police the night before saying that their sun was mentally ill and had threatened to kill them with a knife. He had left by the time police got there, but returned to the house the next morning and police were called again.

"When confronted, Mr. Roke re-fused to drop his weapon," then SIU director Ian Scott said his report on the incident. "After a short chase, instead of continuing to attempt to flee, Mr. Roke turned around and made it clear that he was prepared to be shot by the officers. He approached them in an aggressive manner ignoring all pleas and commands to drop his weapon. The prior deployment of pepper spray proved to be ineffective and none of the subject officers were equipped with a conducted energy weapon."
The inquest was announced Wednesday by Dr. Louise McNaughton-Filion, the regional coroner for Eastern Ontario. A date and location has not been set.
The inquest is mandatory under the Coroner's Act. The inquest will examine the circumstances surrounding the death and the jury may make recommendations to help prevent similar deaths.
